facts.statement: The type specimen of Heintzichthys was discovered in the Cleveland Shale near Cleveland, Ohio, in the United States.
facts.quote: The type specimen was discovered in the Cleveland Shale near Cleveland, Ohio, in the United States.

facts.statement: Heintzichthys lived in what is now Europe and North America during the Famennian stage of the Late Devonian period.
facts.quote: Heintzichthys is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm that lived what is now Europe and North America during the Famennian stage of the Late Devonian period.

facts.statement: Heintzichthys is classified as an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm.
facts.quote: Heintzichthys is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm

facts.statement: Heintzichthys belongs to the family Selenosteidae within the clade Aspinothoracidi.
facts.quote: Heintzichthys is a member of the family Selenosteidae of the clade Aspinothoracidi

facts.statement: Heintzichthys is classified in the class Placodermi.
The parent group of Heintzichthys is the clade Aspinothoracidi.
Heintzichthys lived between 372.15 and 358.86 million years ago during the Famennian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Famennian to Famennian (372.15 to 358.86 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Heintzichthys was described by Whitley in 1933.
The type species of the genus is Heintzichthys gouldii, originally described by Newberry in 1885.
Heintzichthys has synonyms including Dinichthys corrugatus, Dinichthys gracilis, and Stenognathus corrugatus.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Dinichthys corrugatus (Newberry, 1893) Dinichthys gracilis (Claypole, 1897) Stenognathus corrugatus (Newberry, 1889)

facts.statement: A 2022 study by Jobbins et al. suggests that Heintzichthys is a sister taxon to Gorgonichthys.
facts.quote: According to a 2022 Jobbins et al. study, Heintzichthys was found to be a sister taxa to Gorgonichthys.
